note: Correctors (lumacaftor, tezacaftor, elexacaftor, vanzacaftor; galicaftor and GLPG2737 failed) went to patients on chloride rescue in F508del bronchial cells from CF patients.
label: Cystic fibrosis (CFTR correctors)

engagement.confidence_note: Entry opens at 2009, when lumacaftor's first patient trial (NCT00865904) started on these data; the paper was printed in 2011.
engagement.note: Lumacaftor raised chloride secretion in F508del/F508del patient bronchial cells to ~14% of non-CF; the system that took correctors to patients.
engagement.short: Lumacaftor rescues chloride in patient cells
engagement.quote: VX-809 improved F508del-CFTR processing in the endoplasmic reticulum and enhanced chloride secretion to approximately 14% of non-CF human bronchial epithelial cells (EC(50), 81 ± 19 nM), a level associated with mild CF
engagement.judgement: Year 2009 is the proxy for first use. The FDA pharmacology review says these HBE data were in the IND. Abstract-level reading.

engagement.magnitude_basis: sweat chloride change vs HBE chloride current
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Sweat chloride fell by roughly 8 mmol/L. Nasal PD and rectal CFTR maturation did not change.
engagement.note: 28 days of lumacaftor lowered sweat chloride dose-dependently in F508del homozygotes. Nasal potential difference did not move.
engagement.short: Sweat chloride fell; nasal PD did not
engagement.quote: VX-809 reduced elevated sweat chloride values in a dose-dependent manner (p=0.0013) that was statistically significant in the 100 and 200 mg dose groups.
engagement.judgement: This is a pairing, not a stated comparison: the trial abstract only cites the in-vitro work. Scored 'same' with source_calls_it 'partial' because sweat moved and nasal epithelium did not. Keating 2018 (NEJM, HBE and Phase 2 in one paper, elexacaftor) repeats the match, so it is not a new entry.

engagement.magnitude_basis: sweat chloride added by GLPG2737 over the dual
engagement.confidence_note: Interim open-label result in n=10, from a press release (6-K, 24 Oct 2018). NCT03540524 has no posted results. In PELICAN, GLPG2737 on top of Orkambi met a sweat-chloride primary endpoint (press release only).
engagement.note: In patient bronchial cells, adding GLPG2737 raised chloride current above the galicaftor dual. In FALCON F508del homozygotes it added no CFTR activity. Combination design: glpg-2737 given with galicaftor + GLPG2451, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Same-target retrodiction: the HBE triple data were public only after correctors had lowered sweat chloride in patients (2011); it failed to reproduce, so it stays contra.
engagement.short: Third corrector added nothing in patients
engagement.quote: Subsequent two-week treatment with the triple combination (GLPG2451, GLPG2222 and GLPG2737) did not result in additional enhancement of CFTR activity.
engagement.reason: Third corrector's HBE gain absent in patients
engagement.judgement: Judgement call. The model side is de Wilde 2019 (Front Pharmacol, full text): in F508del/F508del HBE cells, the triple GLPG2222+GLPG2737+GLPG2451 gave 'further increase in Cl current' over the duals. Year 2019 is when both sides were public. GLPG2737 and galicaftor are both members. PELICAN's positive result for GLPG2737 is weaker than this miss of the specific additive prediction, and the rules let one contra stand. Elexacaftor's later match ran on the same HBE model, so it cannot reopen the cell.

engagement.magnitude_basis: organoid FIS rescue vs sweat chloride fall
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading: the abstract says 'CFTR-restoring compounds'; that these include VX-809 is from the full text, not verified here. Patient side is Clancy 2012 (epub 2011), already in the tile.
engagement.note: Lumacaftor restored F508del CFTR swelling in patient organoids, two years after it had lowered sweat chloride in patients. Drug basis: lumacaftor (VX-809).
engagement.quote: Function of the CFTR F508del mutant protein is restored by incubation at low temperature, as well as by CFTR-restoring compounds.
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: the organoid assay was first run in 2013, after lumacaftor's sweat-chloride result was public (Clancy 2011 epub), so 'retro', not 'same'.

engagement.magnitude_basis: per-patient organoid FIS vs per-patient sweat chloride change
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (Cell Rep full text returned 403; not in PMC). The split of the cohort between ivacaftor (not a member) and lumacaftor/ivacaftor, and whether the correlation holds within the lumacaftor arm, is not verified.
engagement.population: Mixed CFTR genotypes treated with ivacaftor or lumacaftor/ivacaftor
engagement.note: Per-patient organoid swelling correlated with each patient's sweat-chloride change on modulators. Drug basis: lumacaftor/ivacaftor and ivacaftor alone, pooled. Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
engagement.short: Organoid response tracks individual sweat chloride
engagement.quote: The in vitro organoid responses correlated with both change in pulmonary response and change in sweat chloride concentration.
engagement.judgement: Kept as patient-level. It rests partly on ivacaftor monotherapy, which is not a member; if the lumacaftor/ivacaftor subset alone does not correlate, this entry should be dropped. retrodiction left null: whether organoids were measured before treatment outcomes were known is not stated in the abstract.

engagement.confidence_note: Year 2015 is a proxy: Study 107 (F508del/minimal function) started in 2015 on this selection rule; the review was public in 2018. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.

engagement.population: Non-F508del CFTR variants responsive in FRT
engagement.note: FRT chloride transport <10% of wild type defined 'non-responsive' mutations for tezacaftor Study 107. Drug basis: tezacaftor/ivacaftor. Combination design: tezacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
engagement.quote: in vitro testing (mutations that responded with chloride transport < 10% of wild-type CFTR in the FRT cell Ussing Chamber assay)

engagement.magnitude_basis: FRT ≥10% of normal vs sweat chloride change
engagement.confidence_note: Year is the registry results posting (2024-08-01); the paper stating the FRT-to-trial translation is 2026. Abstract-level reading. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.
engagement.model: Fischer rat thyroid cells expressing CFTR variants (Ussing chamber)
engagement.population: 18 rare non-F508del variants FRT-responsive to ETI (no F508del)

engagement.quote: secondary endpoints of sweat chloride (-28.3 mmol/L [95% CI: -32.1, -24.5 mmol/L; P < .0001])
engagement.judgement: Prospective: participants were enrolled because FRT called their variant responsive (CT.gov). Population is outside the tile's F508del population.

dose.confidence_note: The FDA clinical pharmacology review for NDA 206038 bases dose on clinical exposure-response. No review compares the HBE EC50 with free plasma exposure.
dose.note: Cells gave lumacaftor an EC50 of 81 nM. The dose was set from exposure-response in patients, not from this EC50.
dose.short: Cell EC50 not used to set dose
dose.quote: VX-809 improved F508del-CFTR processing in the endoplasmic reticulum and enhanced chloride secretion to approximately 14% of non-CF human bronchial epithelial cells (EC(50), 81 ± 19 nM), a level associated with mild CF
dose.judgement: Untested: no source compares the cell potency target with human exposure.

dose.note: Rat NOAEL gave a 3–7× margin and dog a 2× margin over the clinical dose. Phase 3 patients were dosed to target with adverse events like placebo. Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
dose.short: Tox margin held at the clinical dose
dose.quote: The incidence of adverse events was generally similar in the lumacaftor-ivacaftor and placebo groups.
dose.reason: Stated tox margin held in Phase 3
dose.judgement: Decision 16. FDA pharmacology review: 'The No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) in the 6-month rat study provided a 3- or 7-fold safety margin compared to the proposed clinical dose on an exposure basis'. Dog NOAEL 2-fold. Lumacaftor's respiratory events (label 5.3) are discussed under safety. Vanzacaftor's rat liver finding at >20× MRHD is scored in safety, because patients reached the target dose and the harm was not dose-limiting.

efficacy.note: Chloride rescue to ~14% of non-CF, 'a level associated with mild CF', was taken as the predictor of benefit.
efficacy.short: Cell rescue read as mild-CF level
efficacy.quote: VX-809 improved F508del-CFTR processing in the endoplasmic reticulum and enhanced chloride secretion to approximately 14% of non-CF human bronchial epithelial cells (EC(50), 81 ± 19 nM), a level associated with mild CF

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ppFEV1 vs HBE % of normal chloride current
efficacy.confidence_note: This is a pairing. The FDA pharmacology review for NDA 206038 states the comparison in its own words: 'The HBE cell data have limited translation to the clinical outcomes in the lumacaftor-ivacaftor clinical development program'.
efficacy.note: TRAFFIC/TRANSPORT: lumacaftor–ivacaftor raised FEV1 2.6–4.0 points over placebo in F508del homozygotes. The predicted direction held, but the gain was modest. Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Year is the 24 June 2014 Vertex topline press release, earlier than the 2015 paper.
efficacy.quote: the difference between active treatment and placebo with respect to the mean absolute improvement in the percentage of predicted FEV1 ranged from 2.6 to 4.0 percentage points (P<0.001)
efficacy.reason: Combination met FEV1 endpoint; modest gain
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call. The FDA reviewer adds '(e.g., lumacaftor has a robust in vitro effect but decreased pulmonary function in CF patients)'. Lumacaftor alone was never tested on a primary efficacy endpoint: Clancy 2012's primary was safety, and Boyle 2014's was sweat chloride on the combination. So the monotherapy miss is recorded here and not scored as contra; a stricter reading would make this cell contra in 2015. Elexacaftor (Keating 2018, Middleton 2019) matched on the same model. Galicaftor+navocaftor+ABBV-119/576 (NCT04853368) missed FEV1 against placebo in cohort 2 (difference 0.9, p=0.40) and was terminated. It is not scored because no published model prediction for that combination was found. Elexacaftor's comparison on this model is now its own track (efficacy 15-16). The galicaftor triple (NCT04853368) stays unscored: cohort 1 met ppFEV1 (+2.6, one-sided p=0.002) and cohort 2 did not (+1.3, p=0.254) on CT.gov, and galicaftor was the backbone of both arms.

efficacy.note: Organoid forskolin swelling assay published; F508del rescue by CFTR-restoring compounds shown before lumacaftor's Phase 3 FEV1 result. Drug basis: lumacaftor (VX-809).
efficacy.quote: Function of the CFTR F508del mutant protein is restored by incubation at low temperature, as well as by CFTR-restoring compounds.

efficacy.confidence_note: Pairing. Dekkers 2013 did not state an expected clinical effect size, so this is direction only. Organoids were not the system the sponsor relied on.
efficacy.note: Organoids predicted lumacaftor rescue of F508del; TRAFFIC/TRANSPORT met FEV1, with a modest 2.6–4.0 point gain. Drug basis: lumacaftor (with ivacaftor). Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Year is the 24 June 2014 Vertex topline press release, earlier than the 2015 paper.
efficacy.quote: the difference between active treatment and placebo with respect to the mean absolute improvement in the percentage of predicted FEV1 ranged from 2.6 to 4.0 percentage points (P<0.001)
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: scored as a pairing because the organoid lumacaftor data (2013) preceded the Phase 3 readout (2014 topline, 2015 paper), so it is not a retrodiction for FEV1.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mean organoid FIS per genotype vs published trial outcome
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The correlation pools lumacaftor/ivacaftor and ivacaftor genotype groups.
efficacy.population: Genotype groups incl. F508del/F508del (lumacaftor/ivacaftor) and gating/residual-function (ivacaftor)
efficacy.note: Organoid responses by genotype correlated with published trial outcomes for lumacaftor and ivacaftor; one F508del/R347P subject responded little in vitro and in vivo. Drug basis: lumacaftor/ivacaftor (VX-809/VX-770); ivacaftor alone also in the correlation. Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
efficacy.quote: In vitro drug responses in rectal organoids positively correlated with published outcome data from clinical trials with VX-809 and VX-770
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: compared against trial results already published. Patient-level because it ranks genotypes, not whether the class works.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: per-patient organoid FIS vs per-patient ppFEV1 change
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only. Not a randomised trial: FEV1 changes are observational on-label responses, not a trial primary endpoint. Lumacaftor share of the cohort not verified.
efficacy.population: Mixed CFTR genotypes treated with ivacaftor or lumacaftor/ivacaftor
efficacy.note: Per-patient organoid swelling correlated with each patient's FEV1 change; ROC accuracy good to excellent. Drug basis: lumacaftor/ivacaftor and ivacaftor alone, pooled. Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
efficacy.quote: The in vitro organoid responses correlated with both change in pulmonary response and change in sweat chloride concentration.
efficacy.judgement: Same caveats as the engagement entry. Kept because it is the stated individual-level comparison the HIT-CF programme was built on.

efficacy.confidence_note: Year 2015 is the Study 107 start, a proxy for first use with a member. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.
efficacy.model: Fischer rat thyroid cells expressing CFTR variants (Ussing chamber)
efficacy.note: Before Phase 3, FRT response ≥10% of normal was the rule for which genotypes tezacaftor/ivacaftor should help. Drug basis: tezacaftor/ivacaftor. Combination design: tezacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
efficacy.quote: in vitro testing (mutations that responded with chloride transport < 10% of wild-type CFTR in the FRT cell Ussing Chamber assay)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: FRT net Cl transport vs 10% threshold vs ppFEV1
efficacy.confidence_note: The modified TEZ/IVA FRT assay was submitted with the NDA after EVOLVE/EXPAND read out; the reviewer checked it against those results. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.
efficacy.model: Fischer rat thyroid cells expressing CFTR variants (Ussing chamber)
efficacy.note: For F508del, ivacaftor alone stayed under the FRT 10% bar and tezacaftor/ivacaftor just cleared it, matching modest FEV1 benefit. Drug basis: tezacaftor (TEZ/IVA vs IVA alone in F508del). Combination design: tezacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
efficacy.quote: for the 508del mutation (for which IVA alone does not provide clinical benefit), the in vitro results for IVA did not meet the 10% threshold while they just met the 10% threshold for the TEZ/IVA combination
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: FDA describes checking 'consistency of in vitro assay findings with clinical efficacy data' already in hand. The review also says the assay does not predict whether tezacaftor adds benefit over ivacaftor.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: FRT ≥10% threshold vs ppFEV1 by mutation group
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text of the bundled review (sources/210491). FDA: the assay 'does not predict whether the addition of TEZ to IVA (Symdeko) will result in additional clinical benefit'. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.

Drug basis: tezacaftor/ivacaftor (Study 107 non-responders: F508del/minimal function). Combination design: tezacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Retrodiction: the modified TEZ/IVA FRT assay was checked for the NDA against Studies 106/107/108 already read out; it repeats efficacy 8.
efficacy.quote: for mutation groups for which there are positive clinical data, the TEZ/IVA combination in vitro result met or exceeded the 10% threshold and those that did not meet the 10% threshold failed to demonstrate clinical efficacy
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level same, called 'partial' because the residual-function responders are also ivacaftor-responsive, so that half rests on the potentiator; the Study 107 negative rests on the tezacaftor combination. regulatory_reliance true: the 2018 Symdeko label extends to mutations 'based on in vitro data'.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: binary FRT ≥10% call; magnitude not correlated
efficacy.confidence_note: No CDER review document for S-002 is posted (nda/2020 and nda/2021 paths 404); label and approval letter read in full. Approval date Dec 2020 from the letter's timetable reference and news reports. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.
efficacy.model: Fischer rat thyroid cells expressing CFTR variants (Ussing chamber)
efficacy.population: 177 non-F508del CFTR variants FRT-responsive to ETI
efficacy.note: FDA extended Trikafta to 177 more variants on FRT data alone (sNDA 212273/S-002, Dec 2020); the label says the 10% call predicts benefit but not its size. Drug basis: elexacaftor (in elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor). Combination design: elexacaftor given with tezacaftor + ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Retrodiction: the label's FRT-versus-response statement rests on elexacaftor trials already read out; the 177 added variants had no patient outcome until 2024.
efficacy.short: Trikafta label extended on FRT alone
efficacy.quote: For individual mutations, the magnitude of the net change over baseline in CFTR-mediated chloride transport in vitro is not correlated with the magnitude of clinical response.
efficacy.judgement: Not a new status: the cell is already 'same' from 2018. Recorded for regulatory_reliance and because it is the regulator's own statement about elexacaftor. 'partial' because only the threshold, not the magnitude, predicts.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: FRT ≥10% call vs ppFEV1 vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry NCT05274269 results posted 2024-08-01 show LS mean difference 9.2 (7.2, 11.3), p<0.0001, matching the paper. In vitro: a rat thyroid cell line transfected with human CFTR variants, not patient tissue.

efficacy.quote: In 445-124, mean improvements were seen in the primary endpoint of percent predicted FEV1 (9.2 percentage points [95% CI: 7.2, 11.3; P < .0001])

patient_trials.quote: In FRT cells, 518 of 620 (84%) rare variants responded to elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor.

efficacy.judgement: The first prospective randomised test of FRT-only genotype selection: the trial ran after the 2020 label relied on FRT. Population lies outside the tile's F508del population.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract and PMC full text (PMC5547155) read. 2017 is first use with a member for patient-level prediction.
efficacy.note: Short-circuit current in each patient's own nasal cell cultures, with lumacaftor or tezacaftor added, as a readout of that patient's correctable CFTR. Drug basis: lumacaftor, tezacaftor (in vitro); lumacaftor/ivacaftor (patients). Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
efficacy.short: Nasal cells measure each patient's rescue
efficacy.quote: The CFTR correctors lumacaftor and tezacaftor significantly increased the ∆IscF/I+V response to about 25% (SEM = 4.4) of the WT-CFTR level and the CFTR apical expression to about 22% (SEM = 4.6) of the WT-CFTR level in F508del/F508del HNE cells.
efficacy.model: Patient nasal epithelial cell cultures (Ussing chamber)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: per-patient HNE corrected Isc vs per-patient FEV1 change at 6 months (R2 = 0.95)
efficacy.confidence_note: n = 8 (7 on lumacaftor/ivacaftor, 1 on ivacaftor, not a member). Full text says nasal cells were sampled before treatment started; whether the assay was read before the 6-month FEV1 was known is not stated. Not a registered trial.
efficacy.note: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor correction in each patient's pre-treatment nasal cells tracked that patient's FEV1 change after 6 months of Orkambi; three FEV1 non-responders had low in-vitro correction. Drug basis: lumacaftor/ivacaftor (Orkambi), 7 of 8 patients. Combination design: lumacaftor given with ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint.
efficacy.short: Nasal-cell rescue ranks individual FEV1 response
efficacy.quote: The level of CFTR correction in HNE cultures significantly correlated with the FEV1 change at 6 months in 8 patients treated with CFTR modulators.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level: cells were sampled before each patient started Orkambi, so this is scored as a prediction, not a retrodiction; the class result was already known in 2015 but the individual responses were not.
efficacy.model: Patient nasal epithelial cell cultures (Ussing chamber)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HBE chloride transport vs ppFEV1 change
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only read. Phase 2, 29-day FEV1; Vertex took elexacaftor, not bamocaftor, to approval.
efficacy.note: VX-659 triple raised ppFEV1 up to 13.3 points (F508del/MF) and 9.7 points added to tezacaftor/ivacaftor (F508del/F508del), as its HBE activity predicted. Drug basis: bamocaftor (VX-659) in VX-659/tezacaftor/ivacaftor. Combination design: bamocaftor given with tezacaftor + ivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Davies 2018 is the first stated same-drug comparison on the HBE model: bamocaftor's HBE activity 'translated' into FEV1 gains. Same-target retrodiction: bamocaftor's HBE data were first public with the trial in 2018, after lumacaftor/ivacaftor's FEV1 result (2014).
efficacy.short: Bamocaftor: FEV1 up to +13.3 as HBE predicted
efficacy.quote: Robust in vitro activity of VX-659-tezacaftor-ivacaftor targeting Phe508del CFTR protein translated into improvements for patients with Phe508del-MF or Phe508del-Phe508del genotypes.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Year 2017 is the Phase 2 (NCT03227471, EudraCT 2017-000797-11) start, a proxy for first use with elexacaftor.
efficacy.note: Elexacaftor (VX-445) triple tested in F508del bronchial cells before its Phase 2. Combination design: with tezacaftor + ivacaftor.
efficacy.quote: We evaluated the effects of VX-445-tezacaftor-ivacaftor on Phe508del CFTR protein processing, trafficking, and chloride transport in human bronchial epithelial cells.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 30334692, epub 2018-10-18). Co-primary endpoints were safety and ppFEV1; both met.
efficacy.note: Elexacaftor triple raised ppFEV1 up to 13.8 points (F508del/MF) and 11.0 added to tezacaftor/ivacaftor (F508del/F508del), as HBE predicted. Same-target retrodiction: corrector FEV1 benefit was public since 2014. Combination design: with tezacaftor + ivacaftor. Co-primary design: safety and ppFEV1, both met.
efficacy.short: Elexacaftor HBE gain translated to FEV1
efficacy.quote: The use of VX-445-tezacaftor-ivacaftor to target Phe508del CFTR protein resulted in increased CFTR function in vitro and translated to improvements in patients with cystic fibrosis with one or two Phe508del alleles.

patient_trials.quote: Elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor, relative to placebo, resulted in a percentage of predicted FEV1 that was 13.8 points higher at 4 weeks and 14.3 points higher through 24 weeks

safety.confidence_note: Year 2009 is a proxy for when the toxicology package supported the first patient trial.
safety.note: Lumacaftor had no target organs in chronic rat or dog studies. Rat respiratory safety pharmacology was clean.
safety.short: No target organs in rat or dog
safety.quote: There were no relevant target organs of toxicity identified in rats.
safety.judgement: Lumacaftor's respiratory events in patients (chest tightness, dyspnoea; label 5.3) went unpredicted by clean rat plethysmography at 250–1000 mg/kg. Not scored: the events concentrate in patients with low FEV1, a CF-airway harm a healthy rat could not show.

safety.confidence_note: The patient liver failures are under Trikafta (elexacaftor), 'a drug that contains the same or similar active ingredients'. Both are class members.
safety.note: Rats showed liver necrosis only above 20× human exposure. Alyftrek carries a boxed warning for fatal drug-induced liver injury at the clinical dose. Combination design: vanzacaftor given with tezacaftor + deutivacaftor, scored on the trial's own endpoint. Tracks are per drug: the fatal liver injury is reported with Trikafta (elexacaftor), not vanzacaftor, and Alyftrek's own transaminase rises had no placebo arm, so the vanzacaftor track is unsettled.
safety.quote: Cases of serious and potentially fatal drug-induced liver injury and liver failure have been reported with a drug that contains the same or similar active ingredients as ALYFTREK.
safety.reason: Liver harm is Trikafta's, not vanzacaftor's
safety.judgement: Judgement call. FDA integrated review: rat target organs were 'stomach (erosion/ulcers) and liver (hepatocellular vacuolar degeneration, multifocal hepatocellular necrosis) at exposures greater than 20 times (males) and 60 times (females)' MRHD; dogs clean to 100×. The model named the organ but misplaced the margin. It is scored here, not in dose, because the target dose was reached and the harm was not dose-limiting. Year 2025 is the public date of the review. The earlier elexacaftor case (Trikafta 2019 LFT warning, no animal liver signal seen on a grep of NDA 212273) was not verified in full.

safety.magnitude_basis: rat/dog target organs vs Phase 3 adverse-event incidence
safety.confidence_note: Orkambi label 5.2: three liver-related serious adverse reactions on drug vs none on placebo, with transaminase rates similar to placebo; rats and dogs were silent on liver. Respiratory events are a CF-airway harm a healthy rat could not show.
safety.note: Tolerability ruling: rats and dogs showed no target organs; in Phase 3 adverse events were similar to placebo. Combination design: with ivacaftor.
safety.quote: The incidence of adverse events was generally similar in the lumacaftor-ivacaftor and placebo groups.
safety.judgement: The 'no relevant target organs' statement is a passing tolerability claim, now scored as a safety prediction. 'partial' for three liver serious adverse reactions without a transaminase excess.
safety.reason: Clean tox held; few liver SAEs
